title: Our Sun and Earth directions agree with NASA JPL Horizons
criterion: Sun within 0.001 degrees and Earth within 0.01 degrees, at 8 places and 300 times each, from the file that the app uses
summary: The largest difference at 8 places and 300 times: Sun 0.000192 degrees, Earth 0.005983 degrees. At times on the 10-minute grid the largest difference is 0.005980 degrees. At times halfway between two grid points it is 0.005983 degrees.
details: Input: data/ephemeris.bin (JPL Horizons API 1.2, ephemeris DE441; COMMAND=301 CENTER=500@399 QUANTITIES=14,15,19,20 STEP_SIZE=10min RANGE_UNITS=KM; frame: Moon mean-Earth body-fixed, east longitude, UTC (last known leap second held for future dates); first 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z last 2029-10-31T23:50:00Z; Horizons response Sat Nov 14 07:18:40 2026; built by packages/pipeline fetch-ephemeris).
Reference: Horizons topocentric apparent AZ/EL (QUANTITIES=4, airless) with CENTER=coord@301, GEODETIC site coordinates at height 0, UTC, same epochs. Seed 20261114.
This checks our conversion and the shipped Float32 binary against Horizons. It does not check the ephemeris itself.
Five sites are fixed test points (four polar, one equatorial); three are catalog sites (marked "catalog").
